close_reason: Added 'Some(NodeType::File) if has_target' arm to the consistency_error match in handle_filenode_set, producing invalidProperties[target]. Regression test set_create_file_with_blob_and_target_returns_invalid_properties uses the correct wire shape for the target field (Vec<String>, not bare string). Committed in a56bd11. Gates: fmt/clippy/test/doc green.
description:
src/filenode.rs:372-389 (nodeType inference) and src/filenode.rs:407-422 (consistency_error matching).

Trigger: client sends FileNode/set create with nodeType absent (or null), blobId=<some-blob>, AND target='/etc/passwd'. The inference at filenode.rs:377-383 prefers blob over target ('if has_blob { file } else if has_target { symlink } else { directory }'). The resulting node has node_type = File, blob_id = Some(...), target = Some('/etc/passwd').

The consistency_error match arms cover:
- NodeType::File if !has_blob → error
- NodeType::Directory if has_blob → error
- NodeType::Directory if has_target → error
- NodeType::Symlink if has_blob → error
- NodeType::Symlink if !has_target → error
- _ → None

There is no arm 'NodeType::File if has_target → error'. So a file node with both blobId and target passes the validation silently.

Bad behavior: the FileNode is created with both fields populated. §3.1 (line 482-490 of the spec around target field semantics) implies these are mutually exclusive (target is only meaningful for symlinks). The backend then stores the conflicting state and a future Get returns a confusing object.

Required: add 'Some(NodeType::File) if has_target => Some(("target", "file node must not have target"))' before the catch-all arm at filenode.rs:421.
title: nodeType inference loses target consistency check when both blobId and target are non-null
